correctness.rationale: Derive the triangle Schur complement with correct magnetic holonomy 2 cos(phi), obtain physical cubic and diagonal resolvent. Quartic discriminant sign proves exactly one continuous band for |cos(phi)|<1; derivative sign eliminates the real cubic branch inside it. m-fold free-convolution atom criterion eliminates all eigenvalues at m>=3, and the algebraic Cauchy transform has no singular-continuous component. At cos(phi)=+/-1 factorization gives explicit endpoints and the m=3 inverse-square-root constant. Standard-library exact rational and group-walk checks replay, but are supporting not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Originality is limited to the all-flux all-higher-branching interval, spectral-type and critical-edge classification: prior Mosseri-Vogeler-Vidal covers m=2; Lux-Prodan covers only m=3 connectivity as a consequence of general free-group topology; published SCOPE007 free powers cover the cos(phi)=0 symmetric slice. residual_risks: No exhaustive global survey of differently named magnetic Husimi cactus / free-additive-convolution calculations is possible; an equivalent all-flux formula may be poorly indexed.
Parts of the result (m=3 no gaps, c=0 power law) are already implied by stronger/specialized prior work and are credited, not asserted as new.

The classification 81Q35 is explicitly the first mathematics subject code in the indexed bibliographic classification for the motivating Lux-Prodan paper; the preprint itself does not label an MSC primary/secondary ranking.

value.rationale: A natural family of magnetic triangle cacti changes from flux-induced isolated spectral atoms at m=2 to no atoms and no gaps uniformly at m=3. The exact all-integer branching/cosine-flux quartic edges and critical inverse-square-root density show a substantial spectral transition, not just an arbitrary finite-parameter example; the exact flux dependence is relevant to density-of-states and magnetic localization questions.
